findings.observation: At the early relative-position sample, the Mario circle is visibly below the head/torso and contains mainly the lower body/legs; the other-player circle is also low. The targets remain recognizable, but this is not accurate body-attached tracking at this sample. The 173.933s and 174.233s samples are correctly centered around their characters.

findings.likelyCause: Nonlinear jump/camera movement between directly viewed0.25s source keyframes; the cause is an inference, not proven by this still review.
findings.recommendedAction: Refine the affected intermediate source keyframe(s), or restrict this short burst to the verified centered portion. Recheck both characters in the encoded corrected local interval. Preserve the source/cut/narration/audio.

findings.observation: The native countdown numeral has faded/disappeared in the late sample while the blue circle and same-start-signal label remain over its empty former location. It does not select a different object, but visible-target tracking should hide during this gap.
findings.recommendedAction: Hide the numeral-target circle during verified digit-free frames, or end the short circle burst before disappearance. Keep the genuine countdown/start sequence and the narration. No fabricated countdown value.

findings.observation: The castle ring targets the actual castle correctly, but its upper stroke crosses part of the original Japanese contextual button-selection hint already displayed on top of the castle. The castle, main palette, source logo, fixed captions and game-name header remain visible.
findings.recommendedAction: If this overlay is locally adjusted, use an arc or lower/side contour around the castle to leave the native contextual hint clear. This is a small UI line crossing, not a wrong target or a cropped source.
